diagnosis_explanation:
Your body has a CMV infection. This virus can spread to many parts of your body. It may have caused a problem in your lungs.

You also have polymyositis. This is a muscle problem. You are taking medicine to help with this. You are getting methotrexate and prednisone.
medication_rationale:
Ganciclovir:
This medicine fights the CMV virus.
Your CMV infection may be causing lung problems.
This medicine is given through your vein.
You may feel nausea or have diarrhea.
Your blood counts may change.
Call your doctor right away if you get a fever.
Also call if you have chills or a rash.
Call your doctor if you have bleeding or bruising.

Advair:
This medicine helps you breathe easier.
It opens up your airways.
You may feel your heart beat faster.
You may get a headache or feel shaky.
Rinse your mouth after using it.

Ibuprofen:
This medicine helps lower your fever.
It can also help with pain.
You may get an upset stomach.
Take it with food if this happens.
Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.
Also call if your stomach hurts badly.
Call right away if you see blood in your vomit.

Tylenol:
This medicine helps lower your fever.
It can also help with pain.
Call your doctor if your skin turns yellow.
Also call if you have upper right belly pain.
Call your doctor if you have dark urine.

Folic Acid:
This medicine helps your body make new cells.
It can help protect you from some side effects.
This is important because of your other medicine.
There are usually no side effects from this.

Methotrexate - stopping:
Your doctor wants you to stop taking this medicine.
This medicine can lower your body's defenses.
Do not take it until your doctor tells you it is safe to start again.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You may feel very tired and weak.
- Your chest might feel sore from the breathing tests.
- It is okay to rest as much as you need.
- You must avoid any strenuous activity.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 10 pounds.
- Eat foods that are easy to digest.
- Call your doctor if you have new or worsening chest pain.
- Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing that does not get better.

**Week 2:**
- Your energy levels may slowly start to increase.
- You can try short walks around your home.
- Keep lifting no more than 10 pounds.
- Continue to eat simple, easy-to-digest foods.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 5 minutes twice a day.
- Call your doctor if you cough up blood.
- Call your doctor if your fever comes back.

**Week 3:**
- You might feel a bit stronger than last week.
- Continue to take it easy and avoid heavy tasks.
- You can increase your walking distance slowly.
- Stick to easily digestible foods for now.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 10 minutes once a day.
- Call your doctor if you have sudden shortness of breath.
- Call your doctor if your cough gets much worse.

**Week 4:**
- You may notice more energy for daily activities.
- You can start doing light chores around the house.
- Keep avoiding lifting anything heavy.
- Continue eating healthy, easy-to-digest foods.
- Your goal this week is to walk outside for 15 minutes.
- Call your doctor if you feel sicker instead of better.
- Call your doctor if you have chills with your fever.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You should feel gradual improvement over several weeks.
- Listen to your body and rest when you need to.
- Keep your activity level light and avoid lifting heavy items.
- Follow up with your doctor as scheduled.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Cannot breathe: Your body needs oxygen now.
- Chest pain that will not stop: Your heart needs help now.
- Signs of stroke: face drooping, arm weakness. Get help fast.
- Uncontrolled bleeding: This is an emergency. Call 911 now.
- Loss of consciousness: You may have passed out. Call 911 now.
- Seizure: Call 911 right away. Do not move the patient.
- Severe allergic reaction: Trouble breathing or swelling. Call 911 now.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever above 101 degrees F: You may have an infection.
- Confusion or disorientation: This is new and getting worse.
- Pain is severe: This pain medicine does not help.
- Cannot keep fluids down: You have not eaten for 12 hours.
- Worsening muscle pain or weakness: This can be serious.
- Wound looks infected: Red streaks or pus is visible.
- Sudden bad swelling: This can mean blood clots.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild pain that is slowly improving: This is expected.
- Questions about a medicine or dose: Your doctor can help.
- Mild redness at wound site: This is not spreading.
- Fatigue that is improving: You are getting better.
- Nausea without vomiting: Try small sips of clear liquid.
